_meta.indication: BRAFTOVI is indicated, in combination with binimetinib, for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation, as detected by an FDA-approved test. Not indicated for wild-type BRAF melanoma.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1:1), active-controlled, open-label, multicenter, two-part trial comparing encorafenib 450 mg daily plus binimetinib 45 mg twice daily vs encorafenib 300 mg monotherapy vs vemurafenib 960 mg twice daily.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with BRAF V600E or V600K mutation-positive unresectable or metastatic melanoma, as detected using the bioMerieux THxID BRAF assay.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) by RECIST v1.1 per blinded independent central review.
pivotal_trials.n: 577 patients randomized; 192 to encorafenib+binimetinib, 194 to encorafenib, 191 to vemurafenib.
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 14.9 months (encorafenib+binimetinib) vs 7.3 months (vemurafenib); HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41, 0.71), p<0.0001. ORR 63% vs 40%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=25%) with BRAFTOVI in combination with binimetinib are fatigue, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and arthralgia. Important toxicities include new primary malignancies, tumor promotion in BRAF wild-type tumors, hemorrhage, uveitis, and QT prolongation.
target_moa: Encorafenib is a kinase inhibitor that targets kinases in the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK pathway, inhibiting BRAF V600E, wild-type BRAF, and CRAF with IC50 of 0.35, 0.47 and 0.30 nM, respectively.

rems.type: There are no safety issues identified that require Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS).

companion_dx_detail: BRAF V600E or V600K mutation detected using the bioMerieux THxID BRAF assay (FDA-approved test).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this NDA.

summary.text: BRAFTOVI (encorafenib) received regular (full) approval as a standard review application, based on a statistically significant PFS improvement versus vemurafenib in the COLUMBUS trial. The combination had orphan drug designation for BRAF-mutant melanoma. No advisory committee was convened.
